does: Cooks butter until its milk solids turn nut-brown and it smells of hazelnuts.

intro.what: Brown butter heats butter until its milk solids colour and develop a nutty scent.
intro.why: It teaches you to watch changes in sound, colour and smell before residual pan heat turns browning into burning.

how: Melt the butter in a pale pan, so that you can see its colour.
Let it foam. The foam is its water boiling off.
Swirl the pan as the foam falls and the solids on the bottom turn golden.
Take it off the heat the moment it smells of hazelnuts, and stop it with a squeeze of lemon or by pouring it out.

cues.text: The sputter dies away just before it browns. Silence means the water has gone.
Golden-brown specks on the bottom and a clear amber fat.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving it in the hot pan, where it goes from brown to black and bitter in moments.
mistakes.fix: Pour it straight over the food, or into a cold dish.

quiz.question: What develops the nutty character of brown butter?
choices: Keeping every solid pale while warming.
Whisking cold butter into hot liquid.
quiz.because: Browned milk solids give this butter its hazelnut-like scent.

quiz.question: Why choose a pale pan for this method?
choices: So you can see the colour of the solids.
So the butter will never darken.
quiz.because: A pale pan makes the change from golden to overdark solids easier to see.

quiz.question: Which appearance matches brown butter?
choices: Golden-brown specks in clear amber fat.
White foam without any coloured solids.
quiz.because: Golden-brown solids and amber fat accompany the nutty scent, before burning.

quiz.question: The butter turned black after being taken off the heat. What would you change next time?
choices: Leave it in the pan until the foam returns.
Cover the pan to retain its heat.
Pour it out of the hot pan promptly.
quiz.because: Residual pan heat continues cooking the solids; pouring the butter out promptly limits further darkening.
